results.headline: Micron, Nvidia, AMD on Watch as Asia's Chip Selloff Sends Warning to Wall Street

chunks.text:
The chip-stock bloodbath that started in Seoul overnight is crossing the Pacific - and Wall Street's premarket screens are flashing red.
SNDK stock is red today. See the chart and price action here.
U.S. semiconductor names extended Monday's steep losses into Tuesday's premarket session, with Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) sliding more than 5% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) and Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) each dropping over 4%, according to Benzinga Pro.
Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), SanDisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) and Intel were also lower in early trading, extending Monday's rout that saw Nvidia fall roughly 5% and SanDisk plunge over 11%.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, tracked by the iShares PHLX SOX Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (NASDAQ:SOXX), shed about 2% in the prior session.

results.headline: Nvidia Corporation - Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence Inc. and NVIDIA Announce Long-Term Strategic Partnership

chunks.text:
Access to NVIDIA's Best-in-Class Vera Rubin Systems Expands SSI's Compute by an Order of Magnitude
SANTA CLARA, Calif. and PALO ALTO, Calif., July 27, 2026 Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI) and NVIDIA today announced a long-term partnership to rapidly accelerate SSI's strategic growth. NVIDIA has additionally made an investment in SSI.
For SSI, NVIDIA's substantial investment combined with access to the next-generation, best-in-class NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform will allow SSI to increase its compute by an order of magnitude. The two companies will also collaborate on the technical advancement of NVIDIA's current and future compute platforms, leveraging SSI's unique insights into the future of AI.
For the last two years, SSI has been quietly advancing a new research direction to unlock a powerful and robustly aligned artificial intelligence. NVIDIA entered this partnership to accelerate SSI's next stage of growth after obtaining rare access into the company's closely guarded research.

results.headline: Taiwan detains Nvidia worker in chip smuggling probe

chunks.text:
(Alliance News) - Prosecutors in Taiwan have detained an Nvidia Corp employee as part of an investigation into the smuggling of the California-based tech firm's artificial intelligence chips to China, a source familiar with the case told AFP on Tuesday.
The man was detained after investigators raided his home and workplace on July 24, the Keelung District Prosecutors Office said in a statement without mentioning Nvidia.
He is suspected of offences including "the falsification of business documents under the Criminal Code", prosecutors said in a statement.
The US restricts exports to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips used to power artificial intelligence systems, designed by industry leader Nvidia.
Officials said in May they were investigating the shipment of "high-end" AI servers made by Nasdaq-listed Super Micro Computer and containing advanced Nvidia chips to China, Macau and Hong Kong, in violation of US export controls.

results.headline: Market Chatter: Nvidia Employee Detained in Taiwan AI Chip-Smuggling Probe

chunks.text:
04:40 AM EDT, 07/28/2026 (MT Newswires) -- An Nvidia (NVDA) employee has been detained by Taiwanese prosecutors as part of an investigation into the alleged smuggling of advanced AI chips to China, Bloomberg reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Bloomberg said investigators searched the employee's home and desk at Nvidia's Taipei office on July 24. A court later approved prosecutors' request to detain the employee, identified publicly only by the surname Chang, on allegations of forgery and breach of trust.
According to the report, investigators are examining whether servers containing Nvidia AI chips were exported from Taiwan using falsified documentation before ultimately reaching China.
Bloomberg said prosecutors have not accused Nvidia (NVDA) of wrongdoing. The report added that the case is one of at least eight investigations across four jurisdictions into the alleged smuggling of Nvidia AI chips as authorities seek to crack down on efforts to circumvent US export controls on advanced semiconductors destined for China.
Taiwan previously detained three individuals in May in connection with the alleged smuggling of Super Micro Computer (SMCI) servers containing Nvidia AI chips to China, Bloomberg reported.
The US government has banned the sale of most Nvidia AI chips to China without official approval over concerns the semiconductors could give Beijing a military advantage.
Nvidia representatives did not immediately respond to MT Newswires' requests for comment.

results.headline: NVDA Down 6% in Two Days: What's Happening to Nvidia's Default Insurance Costs?

chunks.text:
Nvidia Corp.'s (NASDAQ:NVDA) credit default swaps posted their biggest one-day jump on record Monday, a sign the debt market may be losing faith in the AI trade faster than the stock market is.
The five-year swaps, which price the cost of insuring Nvidia's debt against default, jumped roughly 14 basis points to around 82 basis points, according to ICE Data Services. The contracts only began actively trading in November.
The move shows "the credit market noticing something the equity market hasn't fully priced," Pepperstone research strategist Dilin Wu told Bloomberg.
The stock fell 4.99% to $196.51 Monday, shedding roughly $250 billion in market value, once again ceding the title of world's most valuable company to Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL).

results.headline: Nvidia reportedly signs 15-year data center deal in Texas - FT

chunks.text:
Chip giant Nvidia has signed a 15-year lease agreement worth up to $50 billion for a 1 gigawatt data center in Texas, developed by Hut 8. This is reported by the Financial Times with reference to sources.
The agreement is said to secure infrastructure for Nvidia's GPU and means that the company is, in practice, financing the physical environment for its neocloud partners.
In a comment, Nvidia said that they are working with partners in the ecosystem to accelerate the development of efficient AI infrastructure through the DSX AI factory architecture, which serves as a blueprint "for building and operating AI factories".

results.headline: Nvidia Employee Detained in Taiwan as Prosecutors Allege AI Chip Smuggling to China: Report (UPDATED)

chunks.text:
(Editor's note: This story has been updated to include Nvidia's statement.)
Taiwanese prosecutors have detained an Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) employee as part of a widening investigation into the alleged smuggling of advanced AI chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls, a source familiar with the case told AFP on Tuesday.
According to the news agency, the man was detained after investigators raided his home and workplace on July 24, the Keelung District Prosecutors Office said in a statement, without naming Nvidia directly. He is suspected of falsifying business documents, prosecutors said.
In an emailed statement to Benzinga, an Nvidia spokesperson said: "Smuggling is a nonstarter."
"We primarily sell our products to well-known partners, including OEMs, who help us ensure that all sales comply with U.S. export control rules. Even relatively small exporters and shipments are subject to thorough review and scrutiny on both sides of the globe, and any diverted products would have no service, support, or updates," the spokesperson added.

results.headline: Micron, Nvidia fall after SK Hynix plunges nearly 15% as chip sell-off deepens

chunks.text:
Semiconductor stocks fell in premarket trading on Tuesday, extending a rout in chipmakers after another weak session on Wall Street.
- South Korean semiconductor shares tumbled on Tuesday, extending a rout in chipmakers after another weak session on Wall Street.
- SK Hynix plunged more than 14%, while Samsung Electronics fell over 13%.
- Selling followed through to Europe and the U.S. with key chip companies falling in early trade.
Semiconductor stocks fell in premarket trading on Tuesday following weakness in Asia and Europe.
Nvidia was down around 1.2% while Intel and AMD were more than 3% lower. Memory chipmaker Micron dropped nearly 5%.
The moves followed a bout of heavy selling in Asia.
In South Korea, SK Hynix plunged 14.65% at the close, while Samsung Electronics fell more than 13%. Other AI-linked names also saw heavy selling, with Samsung SDI dropping 11.37%, LG Innotek fell 16.29%, Seoul Semiconductor falling 8.78% and LG Chem losing 7.5% at the end of its trading day.

results.headline: Apple Overtakes Nvidia as World's Most Valuable Company

chunks.text:
07:10 PM EDT, 07/27/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Apple (AAPL) surpassed Nvidia (NVDA) as the world's most valuable company on Monday, marking the first time it has closed above the chipmaker since April 2025, CNBC reported.
Nvidia shares fell 5%, giving it a valuation of $4.77 trillion, while Apple shares rose 1% to reach a market cap of $4.95 trillion ahead of its earnings report Thursday, according to the report.
CNBC said Nvidia had held the top spot since June 2025, when it overtook Microsoft, and briefly topped a $5 trillion valuation in October.
Apple shares are up 24% so far in 2026 versus a 4% gain for Nvidia, with investors rewarding Apple's lighter AI capital spending, the report said.

results.headline: Nvidia's Potential $250 Billion OpenAI Financing Deal Is Reviving a 1990s Tech Bubble Habit, Analyst Warns: 'Usually Don't End Well'

chunks.text:
While the structure of Nvidia Corp.'s (NASDAQ:NVDA) potential financing to help OpenAI lease a massive Ohio data center remains unclear, Seaport Research analyst Jay Goldberg expressed caution about such an arrangement.
Goldberg warned that vendor financing can backfire, noting companies have previously hurt themselves by financing customer purchases. He pointed to Lucent Technologies' 1990s telecom financing strategy, which he said ultimately "essentially broke that company," reported MarketWatch.
"These kinds of financing usually don't end well," Goldberg said.
He said the reported arrangement remains unclear, but if it moves forward, he believes it would be difficult to "justify" from Nvidia's perspective.
Jefferies technology strategist Jeffrey Favuzza said investors viewed the report as the clearest and largest example yet of potential circular financing, while noting the market is already familiar with such concerns.

What Happened to Lucent?
In the late 1990s telecom boom, Lucent aggressively used vendor financing, lending billions of dollars to telecom carriers so they could buy Lucent's networking equipment.
The strategy fueled rapid sales and network expansion during the boom, but when many telecom startups collapsed after the dot-com bubble burst, Lucent was left with massive bad debts and write-downs, making its financing model a cautionary tale about supplier-funded demand.
In 2006, it merged with France's Alcatel in a $13.4 billion deal, creating Alcatel-Lucent.
Read Also: Nvidia Stock Falls 5%: How Credit Risk Sharing Is Impacting the AI Trade
AI Financing Model Sparks Debate
On Sunday, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia is in talks to provide a $250 billion financing guarantee to help OpenAI secure funding for a massive AI data center in Ohio that could cost more than $500 billion. The arrangement would also include discussions to finance up to $350 billion in Nvidia chip purchases. Developed by SoftBank Group's (OTC:SFTBF) (OTC:SFTBY) energy unit, the project is expected to deliver 800 megawatts of capacity in its first phase by 2028.

results.headline: Sources: Nvidia's investment in Safe Superintelligence is reported to be $5 billion

chunks.text:
Nvidia is investing $5 billion in the AI startup Safe Superintelligence as part of a strategic partnership with the company, according to sources at Reuters and Bloomberg News.
Finwire reported on the deal already on Monday, but then the size of Nvidia's investment was not yet known.
Safe Superintelligence was founded by OpenAI's former chief scientist Ilya Sutskever.
Through access to Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin platform, Safe Superintelligence is expected to increase its computing capacity by an order of magnitude. According to Safe Superintelligence, the investment will enable scaling up the company's AI research.

results.headline: More Than $1 Trillion Wiped Out as China Chip Fears Slam Nvidia, SK Hynix, Micron and Memory Stocks: ETFs to Watch

chunks.text:
More than $1 trillion was wiped from U.S. stocks on Monday, with over half of the losses concentrated in just six memory-related names as investors dumped the sector on fears that China could expand domestic chip production.
Six Memory Stocks Lose $541 Billion in Value
NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) led the decline, wiping out roughly $300 billion in market value, followed by SK Hynix Inc (NASDAQ:SKHY) with $95 billion, Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU) with $82 billion, SanDisk Corp (NASDAQ:SNDK) with $26 billion, Western Digital Corp (NASDAQ:WDC) with $21 billion and Seagate Technology Holdings plc (NASDAQ:STX with $17 billion, according to data shared by market commentator Bull Theory on X.
Together, the six companies erased approximately $541 billion in market capitalization during Monday's selloff.

results.headline: Nvidia Strikes $500-Billion-Plus AI Infrastructure Partnership With SK Group

chunks.text:
10:42 AM EDT, 07/27/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Nvidia (NVDA) has agreed to expand its partnership with South Korean conglomerate SK Group with a more than $500 billion artificial intelligence infrastructure initiative.
The deal announced Saturday includes a long-term partnership between Nvidia and SK hynix (SKHY) that will provide the US technology giant a stable supply of next-generation AI memory. They will also jointly co-develop next-generation AI memory solutions that include high-bandwidth memory chips intended for AI training, AI agents and physical AI applications.
Also part of the agreement is the recently-announced plan by SK Telecom to build a 2-gigawatt-scale AI cloud in its home country using the Nvidia DSX platform. The infrastructure will also be powered by Nvidia Vera Rubin chips.

results.headline: Naver, Nvidia and Brookfield to expand Korea AI factory infrastructure buildout

chunks.text: Naver, Nvidia (NVDA) and Brookfield (BN) announced a proposed expansion of Korea's sovereign AI factory infrastructure, with planned investments that will grow the initial Nvidia DSX AI factory deployment to 200 megawatts - more than tripling the 55-megawatt buildout announced last month. Naver intends to expand its deployment of Nvidia AI infrastructure to 1 gigawatt. Announced during Korea President Jae Myung Lee's AI Summit visit to San Francisco, the planned 200-megawatt expansion marks a significant acceleration of Korea's national AI ambitions. The expanded infrastructure will be built with the Nvidia DSX platform at Naver's GAK Sejong hyperscale data center in Sejong, South Korea. Nvidia plans to invest $1B into Naver Corp. and Brookfield plans to fund up to $9B for AI infrastructure. Naver will fund the remaining amounts to finance the project. Nvidia's planned investment is subject to customary closing conditions.
